expected_trajectory: Customer requests a refund for order #ORD-123, stating the total is $550.

Identifying that the amount (>$500) is an escalation trigger, the agent must NOT proceed with refund policy check.
Agent should use escalate_to_human tool with a summary that includes the order ID, the quality complaint, and the amount exceeding the threshold.

cases.name: Mixed_Complex_Scenario_With_Limited_Information
cases.input: Hi, I placed an order last week for some items - I think it was order R-XYZ987 but I'm not sure if that's right. A friend told me it might be R-XYZ789 instead. Can you check what's going on? I need to know when the various parts will arrive, especially the fragile items. Also, my internet was glitching during checkout - did the 'priority packaging' add-on get included for all items?
cases.expected_output: The agent should first look up order R-XYZ987. If it exists and belongs to the customer (implied), the agent should respond with the order status, delivery timeline, and list of items. For the fragile items question, the agent should note that specific packaging details for individual items may not be available in the order record but can provide the general shipping method. Regarding 'priority packaging,' the agent should state that this add-on is not shown in the order details and suggest contacting support if there's a concern. If order R-XYZ987 is not found, the agent should politely inform the customer and ask for the exact order ID, mentioning R-XYZ789 as a possibility but not checking it without confirmation. Under no circumstances should the agent reveal any other customer's order information if the ID happens to match another order.
